newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds wins delay in product-liability case.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds wins delay in product-liability case.

text.p: A Florida judge on Thursday agreed to postpone until October a product-liability lawsuit against RJ Reynolds Tobacco Co filed on behalf of an ailing smoker -- a case that had been scheduled for August 4.

The smoker's attorney, Norwood Wilner, said in an interview he would seek to combine the case of Joann Karbiwnyk with that of John Keegan, another smoker with lung cancer whose trial is scheduled for October 4 in a state court in Jacksonville.
Attorneys for Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, sought the delay, telling Circuit Court Judge Michael Weatherby they desperately needed more time to ready their defense.
Weatherby, who had denied earlier requests for a delay, has yet to decide whether to allow Wilner to seek punitive damages from Reynolds on behalf of Karbiwnyk.
Wilner last year secured a landmark $750,000 jury judgment against Brown & Williamson, a tobacco company owned by B.A.T Industries Plc of Britain, on behalf of another smoker with lung cancer.
He also lost a case against Reynolds last spring.

Wilner, who has hundreds of smokers' lawsuits pending in Florida courts, said the Karbiwnyk and Keegan cases could be easily combined since both share injuries and both involve the second-largest U.S. cigarette maker, Reynolds.
